title: Divisorial eigenparameters, finite inertia induction and local pullback data
statement:
For an fs log scheme $X$ with a group action $a$ [def-per-fs-log-group-action] and an ideal sheaf $B$, define $\operatorname{DivisorialBoundary}(X,B)$ to mean that the monoid sheaf of $X$ is isomorphic to the divisorial presheaf on $X\setminus |B|$, compatibly with the structural inclusion into $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. For two ideal sheaves $B,D$ on $X$, define $\operatorname{HasLocalEigenparameters}(a,B,D)$ as follows. For each algebraically closed geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, let $H=\{g\mid gt=t\}$. There are an affine $H$-scheme $W$, an $H$-equivariant etale map $p:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and an $H$-fixed lift $w$ of $t$. Writing $N=|H|$, there is an $H$-fixed primitive $N$-th root $\zeta\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$, with $N$ and all $\zeta^k-1$ for $0<k<N$ invertible. There are functions $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ whose germs at $w$ are a regular system of parameters in the ordinary local ring [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and characters $\chi_i:H\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$ taking values in $\langle\zeta\rangle$, such that $h^*f_i=\chi_i(h)f_i$. The ideals $p^{-1}B$ and $p^{-1}D$ on $W$ are generated by products of distinct members of this same family; the two subsets of indices may differ and may be empty.

Define $\operatorname{HasFiniteInertiaInduction}(a)$ to mean that there are finitely many subgroups $H_i\subset G$, affine $H_i$-schemes $V_i$, and equivariant open immersions $j_i:V_i\to X$ such that the translates $g j_i(V_i)$ cover $X$ and $g j_i(V_i)$ and $h j_k(V_k)$ are disjoint whenever $i\ne k$ or $g^{-1}h\notin H_i$. Each $H_i$ is the geometric inertia of some point of $j_i(V_i)$. This specifies the finite disjoint union of induced actions, including the empty union.

For a rigidification $R$ of $a$ in the sense of [def-per-gabber-modification-data], define $R.\operatorname{HasEigenparameters}(B)$ to mean that the enlarged log scheme has its actual divisorial structure for $R$'s boundary, this boundary is invariant, contains the pullback of $B$, and satisfies the preceding eigenparameter predicate with that pullback and the enlarged boundary. For a cover $f:U\to X$ and a rigidification $R$ of its source action, define $R.\operatorname{PullsBack}(f,B)$ by quantifying over all equivariant strict inert etale maps $q:Y\to X$, where strictness is [def-per-strict-log-morphism] and inertness is [def-per-gabber-modification-data]. There are old and enlarged pullback diagrams in schemes [def-pc-fibre-product], with commuting log squares. The old projection to $Y$ is surjective, strict, inert and etale; the other old projection and the enlarged projection are strict inert etale. The enlarged source is log regular, its action is very tame [def-per-very-tame-fs-log-action], and its boundary is exactly the pullback of $R$'s boundary, with the actual divisorial structure. It is a strict normal crossings boundary on affine open neighborhoods [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and the pulled-back old and enlarged boundaries have local eigenparameters. The map from the enlarged source to the old one is an equivariant scheme isomorphism. No global affineness of an arbitrary pullback source is imposed.
